title: refactor: keep css-modules cross-platform consistency
author: Jungzl
summary: Normalizes `\` to `/` before hashing CSS module paths and adds a string-prefix fallback for relative paths. This changes generated class names for Windows users (and for some relative project_root setups on all platforms), so it's a user-visible hash change, not just a refactor. #1247 does the same normalization more simply.
evidence: Master src/css_modules.rs hashes `diff_paths(...)` with OS separators, no normalization (#541: Windows CSS-module hashes differ, e.g. `.Ot1kIW_foo` vs `.EgL3uq_foo`). #1247 (cscnk52, 2026-05-23): same `replace("\\", "/")` plus drops the is_absolute guard, 6/-7 lines. 1120's new `strip_prefix` branch changes hashes when project_root or the path is relative. No comments or reviews on either PR.
decision: Are we OK changing CSS module hashes on Windows (normalizing separators so they match Linux and macOS), and if so, which PR: #1247 (minimal) or this one?
